text:
Morgan H: quick heads-up — noticed a regression in cross-region tail latency after last night's rollout :rotating_light:
Morgan H: p95 across eu->us region routes jumped from ~210ms to ~380ms, p99 spiked to ~900ms for some routes
Morgan H: looks correlated with the kernel-selection change + new quantization fallback for the small-llama variant
Sasha L: ugh. any idea if it's batching or KV cache behavior?
Morgan H: did a quick flamegraph and token-level profiling. two things stood out:
Morgan H: 1) higher KV cache miss rate on routed requests (misses up ~3-4x). seems like different prefix distributions in EU traffic.
Morgan H: 2) kernel selector sometimes picks the fp16 fallback kernel that has higher per-token overhead for short sequences
Devon R: can you paste the profiling snippet?
Morgan H: sure — pasted below (raw):
```
profile_slice: region=eu, route=/chat, model=small-llama-q4f16
tokens_total=1_240_000
kv_cache_hits=940_000
kv_cache_misses=300_000
avg_token_latency_hit=6.1ms
avg_token_latency_miss=18.4ms
p95_token_latency=22.9ms
kernel_switches=1.9% // where kernel chosen != preferred
```
Morgan H: the token-level breakdown shows miss tokens dominate tail latency — each miss triggers an extra kernel path and memory copy in the fallback path
Nina M: hmm that kernel_switches stat worries me. we introduced a quick heuristic to prefer quantized fallback when memory headroom low. might be too aggressive for routes with high prefix variance
Sasha L: so for routed eu->us traffic we might be picking the wrong kernel and thrashing KV?
Morgan H: yep. also observed more frequent small-batch flushes because the batching heuristic assumes contiguous prefixes — cross-region routing mixes short and long sequences, so batching decisions are suboptimal
Devon R: can we temporarily change routing policy to prefer local model variants until we fix heuristics? reduce cross-region failovers?
Morgan H: already tested a config locally — forcing eu->eu routing for tier-1 reduced p95 to ~230ms, p99 down to ~350ms in the canary window
perf-bot: deploy rollback triggered by morgan_h — rollback: kernel-quant-fallback-2026-03-17-23:42 UTC :white_check_mark:
Sasha L: nice. long term we need better instrumentation in the console: token-level latency by route + kernel path tags
Nina M: Agreed. proposal: add per-token telemetry that tags (region_src, region_dst, route, kernel_variant, kv_cache_hit) and surface as stacked bars in per-route dashboards
Nina M: quick sketch of new metric names we can emit: token.latency.ms, token.kv_hit (0/1), token.kernel_variant (string), route.id
Devon R: can we piggyback on existing aggregation pipeline? we need this to be low-overhead — maybe only sample 5% of tokens initially
Morgan H: sampling is fine. also add a lightweight histogram for token latency buckets (0-1ms,1-5,5-10,10-25,25-50,50+) so dashboard can compute p50/p95 without heavy aggregation
Sasha L: add alert rules: if route.token_kv_miss_rate > 1.5x baseline AND p95 > baseline*1.3 then page oncall
Nina M: I'll PR the schema for telemetry and a Grafana dashboard JSON. will include a per-region failover panel (failover_count / total_routed) and kernel_variant distribution
Morgan H: for immediate triage — we'll keep rollback in place, throttle cross-region routing for experimental models, and roll out the sampling telemetry this week
Devon R: do we want a canary for the telemetry itself? start with 1% of requests, EU only?
Nina M: let's do 2% EU routes for 24h, then 10% if signal looks good
Sasha L: remove the auto-quant-fallback heuristic until we have kernel headroom telemetry in console
Morgan H: documented runbook step in the internal incident doc and attached dashboard link: https://console.redwood/dashboards/token-breakdown?canary=eu-2pct :eyes:
perf-bot: incident incident-2026-03-17-kernel-regression created (severity: P2)
Morgan H: thanks all — staying on this, will post updates here.
Sasha L: ping me when you have the first sampled traces, will add to SLA/route KPIs
Devon R: thanks, oncall will monitor the rollback window :thumbsup:
Nina M: adding unit tests for kernel selector heuristics in my next PR
Morgan H: end of thread — saving traces to /artifacts/1771234567 for postmortem
